title: The conclusion comes out of the quotes
statement: In a modelled reading, the conclusion must emerge from the quoted lines step by step and follow from them, never be reached first and decorated with quotes.
detail: A reading course's judge for modelled reasoning fails a think-aloud whose narration reaches its conclusion before engaging the quoted lines, so the quotes decorate a conclusion reached elsewhere, and a write-up whose conclusion does not follow from the chosen quote, tested by whether a child granting the quote could still reasonably deny the conclusion. It passes one where a child following the narration would see the answer emerge from the quoted lines, step by step, in the procedure's own order (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/authoring/inputs/prompt-packs/reading-g3/judge/model-against-text.md`, lines 6-17). The same judge fails narration that asserts a fact the passage on the page does not contain, and a sentence frame whose 'so' step is a leap the guide never explains.

evidence.quote: the narration reaches its conclusion BEFORE engaging the quoted lines, so the quotes decorate a conclusion reached elsewhere instead of producing it; - the write-up's conclusion does not follow from the chosen quote (a child granting the quote could still reasonably deny the conclusion);
Pass when a child following the narration would see the answer EMERGE from the quoted lines, step by step, in the procedure's own order.
